cf.title: Timeline switching with partial WAL records can break replica recovery

input.subject: Timeline switching with partial WAL records can break replica recovery

verdict_reasoning: The author dropped the posted design (v1 to v3) in message #10, and the replacement, an overwritten_lsn field in the end-of-recovery record, has no patch. Four design points on it are unanswered: replication-ondisk-2, standards-compat-1, prior-attempts-2 and replication-ondisk-3. maintenance-fit-3 asks for a reproducer on a tree with commit 6cf1647; two field reports exist, so that point alone does not stop the review. The goal is a real bug fix, and the list must first agree on a design.

brief.title: Mark incomplete WAL records at timeline switch to stop replica recovery loops
brief.problem: A promotion during a multi-page WAL record write leaves a partial record at the end of timeline N, and the new timeline has no XLOG_OVERWRITE_CONTRECORD marking it. A downstream replica in a cascade then keeps asking for the missing page and loops forever in XLogReadPage. A second report shows a cascading walsender failing Assert("sentPtr <= SendRqstPtr") in a related case.
brief.proposed_design: Before the new timeline starts, the patch writes XLOG_OVERWRITE_CONTRECORD at the end of the old timeline to mark the partial record. It also replaces an assertion in walsummarizer with a check, and v3 makes pg_rewind start its checkpoint search from the target's last checkpoint. After review, the author now suggests leaving timeline N alone and adding an overwritten_lsn field to the end-of-recovery record.
user_visible_surface: New WAL content at a timeline switch: an XLOG_OVERWRITE_CONTRECORD record at the end of the old timeline (v1 to v3).
Proposed new field overwritten_lsn in the end-of-recovery WAL record (message #10, no patch yet).
Changed pg_rewind behaviour when the common timeline ends with an overwritten contrecord (v3-0003).
author_claims: The fix addresses the root cause, while commit 6cf1647d87e7cd423d71525a8759b75c4e4a47ec only treats the symptom.
Writing the marker is safe because no other WAL writes can happen during the timeline switch.
A second poster says the same patch also fixes the cascading walsender assertion and a later PANIC on the replica.
brief.thread_state: Artem Gavrilov objected that writing into timeline N creates a second version of it that can conflict with already archived WAL. The author agreed and floated an overwritten_lsn field in the end-of-recovery record, with no patch or reply since January 2026.
unclear: No patch exists for the overwritten_lsn design, and nobody has said whether replicas, pg_rewind and pg_waldump can read the changed record.
The TAP test does not reproduce the loop reliably, so a reviewer cannot confirm the fix.
The thread does not say which supported branches need a backpatch, or how a WAL format change would be handled there.
The thread does not say how third-party tools that read WAL handle the new record or field.

prior_attempts.title: [BUG] Panic due to incorrect missingContrecPtr after promotion
prior_attempts.quote: For the benefit of anyone who may be looking at this thread in the archive later, I believe this commit will have fixed this issue:
prior_attempts.reason: The patch was not committed because a separate commit, 6672d79, fixed the same issue. Robert Haas pointed to that commit, and the author confirmed it fixes the PANIC. Before that, Kyotaro Horiguchi's debugging of the author's logs suggested the inconsistent WAL came from the primary.
prior_attempts.what_is_different: P3 fixed a stale missingContrecPtr that wrote an overwrite contrecord at a past LSN after promotion. This proposal targets a partial record left at a timeline switch and a cascade replica loop.

objections.title: The stuck replica may never reach the record that carries overwritten_lsn
objections.failure_scenario: A downstream replica has the partial record from timeline N in pg_wal and waits in XLogReadPage for its next page. The overwritten_lsn value sits in the end-of-recovery record at the start of timeline N+1, which the reader has not decoded yet. The replica keeps looping, and the operator sees no change after the upgrade.
objections.argument: Message #2 shows that the loop happens while the reader is still assembling the partial record, before any record of timeline N+1 is decoded. With timeline N left unchanged (message #10), the reader must know to drop a half-read record because of information found later in the stream. That changes how the WAL reader decides where valid WAL ends, a step that earlier reviewers judged risky [P4]. The proposal does not say where in xlogreader or xlogrecovery this decision is made.
objections.author_must_show: At which point does the replica learn about overwritten_lsn before it starts waiting for the missing page, and what keeps a real torn record from being skipped?

precedents.title: Make message at end-of-recovery less scary

critic.reasoning: Message #2 shows the loop happens while the reader waits for the rest of the partial record. Message #10 does not say how the reader learns of overwritten_lsn before that wait. The objection stands without [P4].

objections.title: Changing the end-of-recovery record format blocks a backpatch of this bugfix
objections.failure_scenario: An operator applies a minor release on a cascading standby but not yet on the replica below it. The cascading standby is promoted and writes an end-of-recovery record with the new overwritten_lsn field. The downstream replica, still on the older minor release, misreads or rejects that record and stops following the new timeline.
objections.argument: The entry is tagged Bugfix, and the loop affects released branches, so users will expect a backpatch. Message #10 proposes adding overwritten_lsn to the end-of-recovery record, which changes the WAL record format. Postgres avoids WAL format changes in minor releases because standbys and primaries on different minor versions must read each other's WAL. The thread does not say which branches get the fix, or whether older branches would get a different fix.
objections.author_must_show: How will the overwritten_lsn design be fixed in supported branches without a WAL format change that older minor-release standbys cannot read?

critic.reasoning: The entry is tagged Bugfix and message #10 changes the end-of-recovery record. No message names the branches or says how a replica on an older minor release reads the record.

objections.title: Marking the partial record in the new timeline was dropped once already
objections.failure_scenario: The author follows message #10 and records the overwritten LSN in the end-of-recovery record on timeline N+1. Replicas, pg_rewind and pg_waldump must then treat a page on N+1 as a valid continuation of a record that the new timeline never contains. If the zero-gap problem behind the earlier decision comes back, a replica or pg_rewind can misjudge where valid WAL ends.
objections.argument: Message #1 says the original contrecord work proposed writing XLOG_OVERWRITE_CONTRECORD in the new timeline, and that this was avoided because of concerns about zero-gaps in WAL. Message #10 returns to marking the incomplete record from the new timeline but does not say how that concern is answered. The thread also does not say how a new field in the end-of-recovery record could be backpatched. [P4] was withdrawn partly because reviewers judged extra end-of-WAL logic in the WAL reader too risky for the gain.
objections.author_must_show: How does the overwritten_lsn design avoid the zero-gap problem that led to dropping the new-timeline marker, and how would it reach back branches without a WAL format change?

precedents.title: Make message at end-of-recovery less scary

critic.reasoning: Message #1 records that the new-timeline marker was dropped over zero-gap concerns, and message #10 does not answer them. [P4] must not be used as support: it weighed risk against a cosmetic message change, while this is a bug fix.

objections.title: New design is not shown to fix the cascading walsender case
objections.failure_scenario: An upstream replica's walreceiver rewrites WAL after the primary switches timeline at the partial record. Its cascading walsender then resends data it already sent, so a debug build fails Assert("sentPtr <= SendRqstPtr") and a production build may send divergent WAL that later ends in a PANIC downstream.
objections.argument: Message #5 reports that v1 fixed this case because the marker was written into timeline N. Messages #8 to #10 drop that approach, and the overwritten_lsn idea does not touch what an upstream walsender has already sent. The thread does not say whether this second failure still needs a walsender change, which message #5 considered and set aside.
objections.author_must_show: Does the overwritten_lsn design prevent the cascading walsender from resending rewritten WAL, and which test shows it?

critic.reasoning: Message #5 says the v1 approach repairs the walsender case, and messages #8 to #10 drop that approach. No message says whether the overwritten_lsn design covers the walsender assertion.

objections.title: No case shown that still fails after the existing commit
objections.failure_scenario: A committer takes on a change to timeline switch logic and to the WAL record format. Without a scenario that fails on current master, the committer cannot tell whether the change fixes a remaining bug or repeats commit 6cf1647. The committer would then own the risk of the change with no measured gain.
objections.argument: Message #2 calls commit 6cf1647 a fix for the symptom but does not give a scenario that still fails with it applied. Message #1 says its TAP test does not trigger the loop reliably. The reproducer in message #5 deletes a WAL file by hand. Message #5 does report a real assertion failure, but it does not say whether that report was made on a branch that has 6cf1647.
objections.author_must_show: Which deterministic scenario still loops or hits the walsender assertion on current master, which includes commit 6cf1647?

critic.reasoning: Message #2 names commit 6cf1647 as the current fix, but no message shows a failure on a tree that has it. The test in message #1 is unreliable, and the test in message #5 removes a WAL file by hand.

other_surviving.title: Two different ways to mark an overwritten contrecord
other_surviving.failure_scenario: pg_rewind, pg_waldump, or an external backup tool that handles XLOG_OVERWRITE_CONTRECORD and XLP_FIRST_IS_OVERWRITTEN_CONTRECORD reads WAL from a promotion. It does not check the new field in the end-of-recovery record, so it still treats the partial record as valid. The rewind failure in message #6, or a tool error, then happens again.
other_surviving.argument: Crash recovery marks a partial record with an XLOG_OVERWRITE_CONTRECORD record and a page header flag. Message #10 would mark the same condition after promotion with a field in a different record. Every WAL reader would then need to handle both forms, and message #7 already says third-party WAL tools may break. Nobody in the thread answered that point, and the pg_rewind change in v3-0003 was written for the earlier design.
other_surviving.author_must_show: Why can promotion not reuse the existing overwrite-contrecord record and page flag, and which WAL readers must change to understand overwritten_lsn?

critic.reasoning: Message #10 gives a reason for not reusing the existing record: the end-of-recovery record must come first on the new timeline. It does not say which WAL readers must learn the second form, and v3-0003 targets the earlier design.

refuted.title: No evidence the loop survives the existing fix in 6cf1647d
refuted.failure_scenario: A committer applies the TAP test from message #1 to master, which already has commit 6cf1647d. The test does not reliably reproduce the loop, so nobody can tell whether the patch fixes a live bug or one that is already closed. The committer then owns a WAL change at timeline switch with no failing case it is known to fix.
refuted.argument: Message #2 names commit 6cf1647d as the current fix and calls it symptom treatment, but no message shows a case that still fails with it. Message #1 says the TAP test does not trigger the issue consistently. The walsender assertion in message #5 is reproduced only by deleting a WAL file by hand. In [P3], a patch in this same area was dropped because a separate commit had already fixed the reported failure.
refuted.author_must_show: Which reproducible scenario still loops or asserts on current master with 6cf1647d, and does the test fail before the patch and pass after it?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of maintenance-fit-3. Its support from [P3] also does not hold: [P3] concerned a different PANIC fixed by commit 6672d79, which is a different commit from 6cf1647d.

refuted.title: Overwritten_lsn in the end-of-recovery record changes WAL format for a bugfix
refuted.failure_scenario: A user hits the loop on a supported branch and the fix ships in a minor release. During a rolling minor update, a cascade replica on the old minor release replays an end-of-recovery record from a promoted node on the new release, ignores overwritten_lsn, and still loops. Tools that decode xl_end_of_recovery read the wrong layout.
refuted.argument: Message #10 proposes extending the end-of-recovery record with no patch, and it does not say how old readers handle the bigger record. The entry is tagged Bugfix, so it may need a backpatch, but a changed WAL record in stable branches is normally avoided. Message #7 already flags third-party WAL tools. The thread does not say whether master-only is acceptable for a bug that users meet on released versions.
refuted.author_must_show: Which branches get the fix, and how do a standby on an older minor release and pg_waldump handle an end-of-recovery record with the new field?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of standards-compat-1. The third-party tool point is covered by standards-compat-2.

refuted.title: Proposed bug fix needs a WAL format change it cannot backpatch
refuted.failure_scenario: An operator upgrades the primary to a minor release that writes an extended end-of-recovery record while a standby still runs the older minor. On the next promotion the standby cannot parse the record and stops replaying. If the fix goes to master only, released branches keep the replica loop, and a second fix is needed for them.
refuted.argument: The entry is tagged Bugfix, so users of released branches are the ones affected. The current direction in message #10 adds an overwritten_lsn field to the end-of-recovery record. Minor releases avoid such WAL record changes because standbys are often upgraded after primaries. The thread does not say which branches get the fix or what they get instead.
refuted.author_must_show: Which supported branches would receive a fix, and how does a standby on an older minor release handle the changed end-of-recovery record?

refuted.title: Each WAL consumer must learn the new marker, and failures stay silent
refuted.failure_scenario: A later change to the WAL reader, walsummarizer or pg_rewind assumes that a timeline ends at a record boundary. Nothing in the regression suite catches it because the TAP test does not reproduce the loop reliably. The failure shows up in a production cascade after a promotion.
refuted.argument: v1 changed recovery and walsummarizer. v3 then had to change pg_rewind for a failure the author found only after the first fix (message #6). Message #7 expects third-party WAL tools to break as well. The overwritten_lsn design has no patch yet, so nobody has checked pg_waldump, pg_rewind or the walsummarizer against it. The WAL reader is a fragile area: [P4] was withdrawn because added end-of-WAL logic there was judged too risky.
refuted.author_must_show: Which in-core and external WAL readers must handle the new overwritten_lsn field, and which deterministic test fails if one of them handles it wrongly?

precedents.title: Make message at end-of-recovery less scary

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of standards-compat-2 for the point that every WAL reader must learn the new field. Its own failure scenario is an unspecified future change, and [P4] concerned a cosmetic message change.

refuted.title: Proposal does not show the loop survives the existing fix in 6cf1647d87e7
refuted.failure_scenario: A committer adds new WAL content at timeline switch, or a new end-of-recovery field, to stop a cascade replica loop. If the code from commit 6cf1647d87e7 already stops that loop on supported branches, every WAL reader and tool takes on a format change for little practical gain. This would come to light only after release.
refuted.argument: Message #2 names commit 6cf1647d87e7 as the current fix and calls it a symptom fix, but no message shows the loop on a tree that contains it. The TAP test does not reproduce the loop reliably (message #1). The walsender Assert in message #5 is a separate symptom, and the thread does not say whether the same commit covers it. In [P3], a separate commit fixed the same contrecord problem and the patch was withdrawn.
refuted.author_must_show: Which failure, the replica loop or the walsender Assert, still reproduces on current master with commit 6cf1647d87e7, and what does a user see?

refuted.failure_scenario: A committer takes on a WAL-format change to the end-of-recovery record that pg_rewind, pg_waldump and replicas must all read. If commit 6cf1647d87e7 already stops the replica loop on current branches, the project pays for a format change and an unclear backpatch for a gap nobody has shown still exists.

committability.owner_note: It needs a committer who knows the WAL reader, the end-of-recovery and timeline switch code, and pg_rewind. No committer has posted in the thread.
committability.liability: The owner signs for WAL written at every promotion and for how each replica decides where a timeline ends. A mistake can stall or corrupt standbys, and a changed record format stays for the life of each branch.
committability.author_follow_up: The author posted three versions and accepted the review in message #10. No patch or reply has followed since January 2026.

precedents_retrieved.title: Allow PostgreSQL to perform promote/pause/shutdown operations at end-of-the-wal when the recovery does not reach the recovery target
precedents_retrieved.summary: The proposal stops recovery from promoting at the end of available WAL when the recovery target was not reached, with a new setting (recovery_target_incomplete) to promote, pause or shut down instead. It later split into a second patch that refuses to start WAL replay when the recovery target lies before the restored backup's position, checked against pg_control.
precedents_retrieved.objection: David Steele found the start-point check incorrect: it uses the checkpoint in pg_control, but backup recovery starts from the backup_label checkpoint, and PITR can only start at backup end. The check would accept invalid targets in long backups and reject valid ones, and the last completed xid says little about commit order. He also noted that no consensus existed for the behaviour change, and returned the patch at the end of the CF.

My point is that the
information you are working from (whatever checkpoint happens to be in

precedents_retrieved.title: using an end-of-recovery record in all cases
precedents_retrieved.summary: Remove the check in StartupXLOG() that falls back to a checkpoint when the last checkpoint record cannot be read at the end of recovery. Go further and always write an end-of-recovery record in every recovery case (crash recovery, single-user mode, non-promotion archive recovery), then request a spread checkpoint afterwards.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The visible messages do not show why. The last message reports that the v3 patch no longer applied to xlog.c and asks for a rebase, and the entry was withdrawn the next day. None of the visible messages objects to the design.

precedents_retrieved.title: [BUG] Panic due to incorrect missingContrecPtr after promotion
precedents_retrieved.summary: After a standby skipped a missing continuation record, missingContrecPtr stayed set, so on promotion the server wrote an overwrite_contrecord at a past LSN and later hit a WAL flush PANIC. The patch writes the overwrite_contrecord only when missingContrecPtr is ahead of the last WAL record, and adds a TAP test.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The patch was not committed because a separate commit, 6672d79, fixed the same issue. Robert Haas pointed to that commit, and the author confirmed it fixes the PANIC. Before that, Kyotaro Horiguchi's debugging of the author's logs suggested the inconsistent WAL came from the primary.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: For the benefit of anyone who may be looking at this thread in the archive later, I believe this commit will have fixed this issue:

precedents_retrieved.title: Make message at end-of-recovery less scary
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch makes the startup process treat a zero-length record, followed by zeroed bytes up to the page boundary, as the normal end of WAL. Recovery then reports "reached end of WAL" at LOG level, with the old invalid-record text as DETAIL, and reports real corruption as WARNING.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Reviewers objected that the patch changes how the WAL reader decides where valid WAL ends, not only the message text. Aleksander Alekseev said zeroed blocks from hardware failure or a bad backup could then pass as a clean end of WAL. Michael Paquier judged the header validation, empty-page and record-read changes too risky for the gain, given recent bugs in this code. The author agreed the end-of-WAL check is heuristic and withdrew the patch.

precedents_retrieved.key_quote: The error stack in the WAL reader is complicated enough that making it more complicated as the patch proposes does not sound like not a good tradeoff to me to make the reports related to the end of WAL cleaner for the end-user.

precedents_retrieved.title: libpq should append error messages, not overwrite
precedents_retrieved.summary: Tom Lane proposed that libpq always append to conn->errorMessage during connection setup and query execution, instead of overwriting it, with only a few defined points that clear it. A second patch labeled each part of the error with the server and port being tried when several hosts are listed.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Michael Paquier returned the patch with feedback because the thread had no activity after August and the patch set no longer applied cleanly. Before that, Robert Haas objected that reporting failures from every host adds noise: when the first host is down and the second rejects a password, the user only needs the password error. Tom Lane did not accept this, and the disagreement was not resolved.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
The last status of this patch comes from August, which has been
unanswered.  So I am marking the patch as returned with feedback.

precedents_retrieved.title: Add timeline to partial WAL segments
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds the timeline that a promoted server switches to into the name of the .partial WAL segment it archives, for example 000000010000000100000001.00000002.partial. This prevents archive conflicts when several promotions in HA setups produce the same .partial file; prioritizing .history files in the archiver was proposed alongside it.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The author stopped working on it. After discussion, Michael Paquier agreed with a revised scheme in which pg_receivewal would also use the timeline-suffixed name. The author then marked the patch Waiting on Author because it needed more work, and no new version followed for about 20 months. Robert Haas and Michael Paquier also objected to back-patching the naming change into minor releases, but that did not decide the entry.

precedents_retrieved.title: skip replication slot snapshot/map file removal during end-of-recovery checkpoint
precedents_retrieved.summary: Skip the enumeration and removal of logical replication snapshot (.snap) and mapping (map-) files during the end-of-recovery checkpoint, so the server becomes available sooner, and leave the files to the next regular checkpoint. A GUC could control this, with the current behavior as the default.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Nathan Bossart argued that skipping the files only at end of recovery does not solve the problem, because regular checkpoints stay slow and the shutdown or end-of-recovery checkpoint can still take a long time. He proposed moving these tasks out of checkpointing, which another thread was already discussing. The author agreed to handle the problem in that thread and withdrew this entry.

precedents_retrieved.title: pg_rewind with cascade standby doesn't work well
precedents_retrieved.summary: When a cascading standby replays the end-of-recovery record of its upstream's promotion, the patch has it request an immediate restartpoint. The control file then shows the new timeline, so pg_rewind can use the standby as source right away instead of reporting "same timeline". An earlier version set minRecoveryPoint and minRecoveryPointTLI in xlog_redo, but that broke crash recovery.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The last review came in July 2024 and no author reply is visible before the entry was returned. That review found that v3 no longer applied to master. It asked whether making WAL replay wait for the restartpoint hurts performance, and noted the behaviour change was not documented. It also proposed a less invasive fix, where pg_rewind detects the case and runs a checkpoint on the standby.

kestrel, rorqual and calliphoridae, the assertions checking that a TLI
history file should not exist when created by a WAL receiver have been
failing, and switching to durable_rename() over durable_rename_excl()
would cause the newest TLI history file to overwrite the existing one.
We need to think harder about such cases, so revert the new logic for
now.

Note that all the failures have been reported in the test
025_stuck_on_old_timeline.

precedents_retrieved.objection:
This reverts commit eafdf9de06e9b60168f5e47cedcfceecdc6d4b5f
and its back-branch counterparts.  Corey Huinker pointed out that
we'd discussed this exact change back in 2016 and rejected it,
on the grounds that there's at least one usage pattern with LIMIT
where an infinite endpoint can usefully be used.  Perhaps that
argument needs to be re-litigated, but there's no time left before
our back-branch releases.  To keep our options open, restore the
status quo ante; if we do end up deciding to change things, waiting
one more quarter won't hurt anything.

Rather than just doing a straight revert, I added a new test case
demonstrating the usage with LIMIT.  That'll at least remind us of
the issue if we forget again.

precedents_retrieved.objection:
This reverts commit 728f86fec65537eade8d9e751961782ddb527934.

The signal handling was a few bricks shy of a load in that commit,
which made the walreceiver non-responsive to SIGTERM while it was
waiting for the connection to be established. That prevented a standby
from being promoted.

Since it was non-essential refactoring, let's revert it to make v16
work the same as earlier releases. I reverted it in 'master' too, to
keep the branches in sync. The refactoring was a good idea as such,
but it needs a bit more work. Once we have developed a complete patch
with this issue fixed, let's re-apply that to 'master'.

roaster_notes.note: The v1-v3 design of writing into timeline N was settled in messages #7-#10, where the author agreed it conflicts with archived WAL, so it is not raised here. The thread itself cites two earlier discussions (message #1) and commit 6cf1647d (message #2).
The concern about writing into an already archived timeline N was raised in message #7 and accepted by the author in message #10, so it is not repeated here.
The v1-v3 design of writing into timeline N is not raised again here, because message #7 objected to it and message #8 accepted that.

The proposal changes WAL written at promotion, the replica's handling of a timeline switch, and pg_rewind's checkpoint search, and only superusers or operators start these actions. No new privilege, role, setting, information exposure, or path that lets an unprivileged user cause a denial of service is involved.
No committer has posted in the thread in the ten months it has been open. Only a non-committer reviewer is engaged, so ownership of the recovery and pg_rewind changes is open.
Only one point fits this angle. No extension or external tool can fix how the server writes WAL at a timeline switch, so core placement is not in question.
This is a bug fix, so the usual demand test does not apply. Two posters report two field failures in cascading setups, and a reviewer is engaged.
